LESSON: POETRY 2.2.1 APPRECIATION OF POETRY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: ORAL NARRATIVES: INTRODUCTION Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Sugge
Topic 2.2: Poetry 2.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Poetry 2.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry, part of ORAL NARRATIVES: INTRODUCTION Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Sugge in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How are poems classified? 2. How can we make the performance of poems enjoyable?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Poetry 2.2.1 Appreciation of Poetry together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: This is enhanced as the learner explores characteristics and structure of different

types of poems.

● Learning to learn: This is promoted when the learner reflects on their own work as they discuss and share information

on different types of poems.

Values:
Unity: This is developed when the learner cooperates with others to perform different types of poems and presents their

performances in and out of class.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship education: This is enhanced as the learner shares their findings in class to promote social cohesion.
